groups.facts: Three separate parallel finite planar networks are shown in an oblique view. Each contains FIVE adjacent hexagonal faces: upper/lower planes have three in the rear row and two in the front row; middle plane has two rear and three front. Dark filled atom dots occupy face vertices; solid in-plane edges share vertices/edges. Upper and lower patches correspond; the middle patch is offset. No numbered atoms, axes, unit labels, calibration, arrows, dashed edges or extra cycles.

Seven visible roughly vertical solid correspondence columns span upper-middle-lower heights: three close at image left, two close near the center, one near image-right-middle and one far-right. The leftmost and far-right middle-level dots extend outside the middle five-face patch and connect back to its boundary. Source hatching fills hexagonal interiors but is print shading, not additional lattice edges.

uncertainties: Dense black hatching merges several interior dot outlines and bond crossings. Five closed cells per plane and seven correspondence columns are visually distinguishable; separate atom-circle outlines at overlapped crossings are not all individually measurable.

Reconstruction uses the minimal connected five-hexagon graph (19 distinct face vertices per plane), with the two source middle boundary guide dots. Native assertions prove that reconstruction, not a pixel-measured count of every hidden dot. Independent source/geometry review must resolve any disagreement before promotion.

Source is an uncalibrated oblique schematic. Intrinsic regular hexagons and approximate spacing are constructed in unmeasured author space and projected; no pixel length is presented as a physical distance.
modernAdditions: Clean unhatched faces and muted solid layer guides improve separation. Guides are geometric correspondence marks, not a claim of new strong interlayer covalent bonds. No new numerical readings or visible construction anchors.
